cards.text: Meet Jeremiah, the LORD's prophet. Right before this, God told the people to ask where the good way is and walk in it, and they said they will not walk in it (Jeremiah 6:16). Now the word of the LORD comes to Jeremiah, and God tells him where to stand.

cards.question: God tells Jeremiah to stand in the ___ of the house of the LORD and proclaim His message.

cards.text: Every person of Judah coming through those gates to worship the LORD would have to walk right past him. That's like grabbing the mic at the office front door on Monday morning, and NOBODY is sneaking by.
The message comes from the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, and it starts with a command: correct your ways and deeds.

cards.question: God tells the people of Judah that if they correct their ways and deeds, He will let them live in this place.
God warns the people at the temple gate not to trust in deceptive words. What are those words all about?

cards.text: God even spells out the words: 'This is the temple of the LORD, the temple of the LORD, the temple of the LORD.' That's like telling everybody, "I've got a gym membership, I've got a gym membership, I've got a GYM MEMBERSHIP," while the card is still in the wrapper.

cards.question: God explains what really correcting their ways and deeds looks like. What's the first thing He names?

answers.text: Bringing more sacrifices to the temple
Repeating the prayers of their fathers

cards.question: God tells the people they can keep following other gods, as long as they treat the foreigner, the fatherless and the widow well.

cards.text: God's list goes on: no more oppressing the foreigner, the fatherless and the widow, and no more shedding innocent blood in this place. Do all that, and God will let them live in this place, in the land He gave their fathers forever and ever.

But God says they keep trusting those deceptive words, and it gets them nowhere. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer with dead batteries that swore they still had a little charge left, and I believed them EVERY single time.

cards.question: God asks: will they steal, murder, commit adultery and perjury, burn incense to Baal, a false god, and follow other gods they have not known, then come stand before Him in the house that bears His Name and say what?

answers.text: They're delivered so they can keep going
They're sorry and ready to change
They're poor and need His help

cards.question: God asks if His house, which bears His Name, has become something in their sight. What picture does He use?

cards.text: Then the LORD declares, "Yes, I too have seen it…" Much later, Jesus uses the words "a den of robbers" in the temple courts (Matthew 21:12-13).

Then God tells the people to go to Shiloh, where He first made a dwelling for His Name, and see what He did to it. Friend, that's one road trip where you can tell from the driveway you are NOT gonna like the view.

cards.question: God says He did what He did to Shiloh because of the wickedness of His people Israel.
God says He spoke to the people of Judah only one time.
Because they would not listen when He spoke again and again, God says He will do to the house they trust in what He did to ___.
After warning about the house they trust in, what does God say He will do with the people of Judah themselves?

answers.text: Cast them out of His presence

cards.text: And they won't be the first, because God already cast out all their brothers, all the descendants of Ephraim, Joseph's son (Genesis 41:52). Hold on to your apron, friend, because the LORD has more to say.
